title: Hierarchical LLM-referee pipeline with anchor-rescaling for regression alerts
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: Build a hierarchical judgment pipeline for post-deploy quality checks that combines a lightweight rule-based prefilter, an ensemble of LLM judges, and an anchor-rescaling layer to produce robust, calibrated regression signals tied to config/model changes. Background: Current LLM-as-judge signals are sensitive to prompt phrasing and drift between judge and production model variants, producing noisy alerts during rollouts. This ticket proposes an anchor-driven rescaling strategy and a two-stage judge orchestration to reduce false positives while preserving sensitivity to real regressions. Goals: 1) Reduce noisy regression alerts by >40% on internal rollouts while maintaining >90% detection of seeded regressions. 2) Produce per-cohort calibrated scores with confidence intervals and a scalar severity score useful for automated gating (canary/rollback). 3) Integrate the pipeline into the existing rollout webhook so alerts are emitted as part of config/model rollouts. High-level approach: - Stage 0 (Prefilter): A deterministic checker that filters trivially-passed examples (formatting, exact-match safety failures) to reduce judge compute. - Stage 1 (Ensemble Judges): Run 3 lightweight LLM judges with diverse prompts and temperatures to capture different sensitivities. Use rank-aggregation (Borda-style) rather than simple averaging to reduce outlier influence. - Anchors & Rescaling: For each cohort, include a small set of anchored control prompts (gold and synthetic) that are unchanged across rollouts. Compute anchor-delta per judge and apply a logistic rescaling to map judge raw scores into a calibrated severity scale. - Cohort-level stats: Compute bootstrap CIs for cohort mean severity and run a two-sided sequential test to detect regressions early. - Alerting & Severity: Emit multi-level alerts (info/warn/critical) with suggested actions (canary pause, scale-down, rollback). - Human-in-loop: Provide an adjudication UI link (Console) with judge outputs and anchor diagnostics for triage. Trade-offs considered: - Extra latency/compute for ensemble judges vs. lower false-positive rate; mitigated by prefilter and sampling. - Anchors reduce sensitivity to benign drift but require maintenance of anchor sets per cohort. - Using non-deterministic LLM judges increases variability; rescaling and rank aggregation aim to stabilize outputs. Long-term: Investigate learning-to-rank calibration layers (small calibrated model) and continuous anchor refresh strategies.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline runs automatically on every config/model change and within the existing rollout CI window
False positive rate on historical rollouts reduced by at least 40% (measured on internal benchmark)
Seeded regression detection >= 90% across prioritized cohorts
Per-cohort severity score + 95% bootstrap CI computed and surfaced in Console
Automated alerting with three severity tiers and recommended rollback action is implemented
success_metrics: Reduction in pager noise attributed to eval alerts (percent)
>80% of triaged alerts resolved without engineer intervention due to clear anchor evidence

technical_notes: Anchor design: per-cohort set of 30 prompts (10 gold, 20 synthetic) covering typical failure modes; stored as immutable artifacts
Rescaling: logistic transform using median anchor-delta; fall-back to global baseline when cohort anchor variance is low
Ensemble: three judge configs (low/high temp + contrastive prompt) to diversify failure modes
Stat test: sequential bootstrap with alpha control to minimize early false alarms during canary rollouts
Storage: results saved in evals DB with linkage to rollout_id, model_version, and config_hash
Ops: quota budgeting for judge runs; prefiler reduces judge calls on high-volume routes
